content.user_title: Integrate NodeMaven SDKs in Python, Rust, and Go
content.value_statement: Proxy integrations require correct parameters, credentials, and session handling across languages. This skill provides NodeMaven SDK examples for proxy configuration, connectivity checks, and account clients.
actual_capabilities: Explain SDK installation and environment-based credential configuration for Python, Rust, and Go.
Show validated proxy parameters, normalized location values, and proxy URL construction.
Map proxy settings to requests, httpx, Playwright, reqwest, and Go HTTP clients.
Show sticky sessions, parameter replacement, and per-worker session pool creation.
Explain connectivity checks, refusal results, and language-specific error handling.
Introduce account clients, catalogue validation, city pagination, and credential-safe response handling.
limitations: The skill contains documentation and examples, not bundled SDK implementations or an executable service.
Live checks and account operations require installed SDKs, network access, and appropriate NodeMaven credentials.
Detailed gateway rules and account endpoint behavior are delegated to related skills.
Examples do not independently verify current package behavior, proxy availability, or exit IP uniqueness.

use_cases.title: Connect a Python application
use_cases.description: Adapt proxy configuration for requests, httpx, or Playwright while using environment credentials and handling validation errors.

use_cases.title: Allocate Rust worker sessions
use_cases.description: Configure reqwest with NodeMaven proxies and assign separate session identifiers to concurrent workers.

use_cases.title: Check Go proxy connectivity
use_cases.description: Configure an HTTP transport and distinguish proxy refusals from check errors without exposing credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Python proxy integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a minimal NodeMaven Python proxy setup for requests using environment credentials and country us. Explain required packages without displaying secrets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: configure a first proxy client.

prompt_templates.title: Add a sticky browser session
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt my Python Playwright configuration to use a NodeMaven sticky session named order4417. Validate parameters and keep credentials out of logs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: preserve a session across browser requests.

prompt_templates.title: Configure concurrent Rust workers
prompt_templates.prompt: Show NodeMaven Rust setup for 50 reqwest workers with one session identifier per worker. Handle SDK errors and distinguish proxy refusal from check failure.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate proxy sessions for concurrent workers.

prompt_templates.title: Review Go proxy and account integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Go NodeMaven integration for HTTP transport, session allocation, check results, and account client credentials. Identify missing checks and prevent credential-bearing responses from reaching logs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review an existing integration and its credential handling.

output_examples.input: Which Python calls configure a sticky proxy for Playwright?
output: Create a Proxy with validated parameters and credentials from NODEMAVEN_LOGIN and NODEMAVEN_PASSWORD.
Use session with a valid identifier such as order4417 to configure a sticky session.
Use playwright to obtain server, username, and password fields for the browser configuration.
Do not log the resulting credential-bearing configuration.

output_examples.input: How should I handle a proxy connectivity check in Go?
output: Call Check with the request context when a live connectivity check is authorized.
Inspect the returned check result for a proxy refusal.
Handle the error separately when the check receives no answer.
Keep proxy credentials out of diagnostic output.

output_examples.input: Can I print the account response to inspect remaining traffic?
output: Avoid printing the full account response because it can include plaintext proxy passwords.
Select only the required traffic fields and exclude credential fields from logs or shared output.
Use NODEMAVEN_APIKEY for account access, separately from proxy login credentials.

best_practices: Keep proxy credentials and account API keys separate, and never log full account responses or authenticated proxy URLs.
Validate parameter names, value formatting, and session identifiers before making network requests.
Handle refusal results separately from connectivity errors, and assign a session identifier to each worker.
anti_patterns: Printing complete account responses, browser proxy configurations, or authenticated URLs.
Assuming proxy construction performs a live check or guarantees a distinct exit IP for every worker.
Copying examples without handling errors or supplying the appropriate environment credentials.

faq.question: Which languages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It documents NodeMaven SDK usage in Python, Rust, and Go, including corresponding installation commands and common proxy operations.

faq.question: Does building a proxy contact the network?
faq.answer: The documentation states that proxy construction opens no socket. Connectivity checks and account API operations use the network.

faq.question: Which credentials are required?
faq.answer: Proxy setup uses NODEMAVEN_LOGIN and NODEMAVEN_PASSWORD when credentials are not supplied directly. Account clients use the separate NODEMAVEN_APIKEY secret.

faq.question: How do sticky sessions and worker pools differ?
faq.answer: A sticky session uses a chosen identifier for a flow. Session pools generate identifiers for workers but do not independently verify distinct exit IPs.

faq.question: Can account responses contain passwords?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill warns that me and sub-user calls return plaintext proxy passwords. Select required fields instead of printing or sharing complete responses.

faq.question: Does this skill install or run the SDK automatically?
faq.answer: No executable installer is bundled. The skill provides installation commands and usage examples for an assistant to adapt to your project.
